cells.tense: You are the one deciding what is finished, here, with your hands on it.
cells.ask: Hand over one task today with a clear finish and no instructions, and let the outcome stand as it lands.
cells.core:
You know something few people learn: carrying a thing to its end and then opening your hands. Not walking away early, not holding on past the finish. Somewhere in your life this has gone well and you noticed it — work that needed finishing got finished, and when it was done you let it be done.

Watch how this runs now. You move through the day adding and subtracting without much announcement. That adjusting is the skill itself, and it's holding steady because you let the work answer for itself. The next thing it can feed is smaller and earlier than what you just finished, and it will not need your protection.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things and you know when to open your hands.
cells.verb: carrying a weight all the way to the moment of putting it down
cells.place: a moving balance point that is adjusted by hand, not held still

cells.tense: You are gripping the ending before anyone has asked you to end it.
cells.ask: Pick one plan you can't stop rehearsing and speak it out loud as a plan rather than a verdict.
cells.core:
You're finishing things that aren't near finished. The release is already happening in your head — how it ends, who takes over, what happens after — and your body is standing in a room the day hasn't built yet. So you push. A little harder on the schedule, a little more explanation than anyone needed, a hand on something that was going to stay put on its own.

The push is spending the very thing that made you good at this. When release runs ahead of the finish, nobody gets to complete anything, including you. There's a version where the ending comes when the work is actually done, and you are not standing there bracing for it.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing endings that haven't arrived.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a finish you already crossed.
cells.ask: Say the words "it's done" about one finished thing, to yourself or someone, and mean it without adding a clause.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like a handover that stays a handover: you finish what you started, you set it down, and later you can point to it as something that stands. You built it, held it, released it, in that order, and the release arrived as the end of the job rather than as a loss.

What's happening instead is that you finished something real and stepped out from behind it. Your hands keep hovering over a balance that isn't wobbling. Whether you can do this was the question you answered, and effort was never the one. Do one small thing this week that builds and holds — something you can point to and say it stands — and the finishing will come with it.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it. You stopped calling it yours.

cells.tense: You are already deciding what to release next; you just haven't claimed the deciding as yours.
cells.ask: Name one thing that ended well and say aloud what you did to let it end rather than what happened to you.
cells.core:
Here is what this looks like when it's working: someone takes something up, finishes it, sets it down cleanly — and says so out loud. You hand something over and it goes smoothly; you step out of a role and the next person isn't flailing. That part is visible from the outside. You've been describing it as just how it went, the way a thing goes when nobody is steering it.

You pick what's finished and you let it go, and you don't call that a skill. It runs all day at a size you don't notice, adding and subtracting without a word to anyone. Say out loud that one ending was your doing, and the care underneath it stays what it is: care.
cells.sheetLine: You arrange clean endings and call them nothing special.
